reader.requirement: At --std 85 the compiler must refuse an INITIALIZE statement whose identifier-1 or identifier-2 (the REPLACING sending operand) references an index data item (USAGE INDEX, elementary or a subscripted table element of one); a group that merely CONTAINS an index data item is a legal identifier-1, its index data items left unaffected (§1985:VI.6.17.4 GR3).

edition-consulted.switches: the post-bind INITIALIZE gate asks edition rows for the 1985 ODO prohibition (SR4, GateCobol85VariableOccurrence) and the figurative-to-numeric MOVE rows; it does not touch the index screen, which is upstream in the binder and identical at every edition

reader.edition-search: grep -n -i 'Edition|DialectLevel|CobolVersion|ConstructRegistry' InitializeBinder.cs (only ctx.Edition.Error, a diagnostic sink); read ClassOfPlace and MoveTable16.SenderClassRefusal/Sr1ClassRefusal (no edition term); grep GateInitialize in VersionConformancePass
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: 1985 SR5 and 2023 SR1/SR4 both exclude index-class identifier-1 and identifier-2; the probes print identical diagnostics at 85 and 2023
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witnesses exercise the index identifier-1 and the index REPLACING sender; the subscripted index table element, an index data item as the second of several identifier-1 operands, and the positive group-containing-an-index case are not exercised by them

probes.printed: COBOL2030 on INITIALIZE IX1, on INITIALIZE TI (2) (subscripted index table element), on INITIALIZE GN IX1 (second operand); COBOL2031 on INITIALIZE G REPLACING NUMERIC DATA BY IX1; same at 2023
[000][   ][3] then [777]: INITIALIZE G of a group holding GI USAGE INDEX compiles, GN/GX reset, GI keeps occurrence 3; INITIALIZE T REPLACING NUMERIC over an INDEXED BY table runs
COBOL1637: 'K' is an index-name, which is not an identifier
probes.expected: refused (INITIALIZE takes identifiers; an index-name is not one)

reader.notes: Identifier-1 is screened by the class classifier on the resolved receiving place, identifier-2 by MOVE's SR1 sending class refusal; neither consults the edition, which is right because the 1985 rule and the 2023 rules agree.
